target.projectDescription: D-Tale is the combination of a Flask back-end and a React front-end for viewing & analyzing Pandas data structures (dtale/ package). It runs as a local web server (dtale.app.show / build_app, DtaleFlask(Flask) at app.py:120/:315), from the command line (dtale.cli.script main click command with pluggable data loaders under dtale/cli/loaders/), inside Jupyter notebooks, and can be embedded in Django (dtale/django/dispatcher.py WSGI mounting) or Streamlit. Attacker-relevant input surface: the Flask HTTP API (~85 @dtale.route endpoints in views.py; authentication exists via dtale/auth.py but is DISABLED by default: global_state.AUTH_SETTINGS = {'active': False, ...} at global_state.py:38, requires_auth only short-circuits when active, applied through @app.before_request at app.py:457-458). The data-loading endpoints accept URLs: /web-upload (views.py:3921) reads 'url' and 'proxy' straight from the query string and forwards them to the CLI data loaders, which fetch remote http(s) resources through dtale.cli.clickutils.handle_path (clickutils.py:239-249 -> requests.get at :244). Outbound network access: requests.get is the only real HTTP-client call in the tree (5 sites).

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face a Flask HTTP API with ~85 routes that is UNAUTHENTICATED by default (auth.py requires_auth only gates when [auth] active is configured in dtale.ini; global default is False). Input is read (1) from the query string through five wrapper functions get_str_arg/get_int_arg/get_float_arg/get_bool_arg/get_json_arg (142 call sites: views.py 120, column_analysis.py 20, query.py 2; each wrapper is 'r.args.get(name)' in utils.py:114-204); (2) directly via request.args.to_dict() (views.py:1429, :3799, :3814, :3825); (3) from JSON request bodies via request.json.get(...) / bare request.json (views.py:1677, :1785, :1791, :3991, :4008, :4153); (4) from form bodies via request.form.get/[...] / membership (views.py:3871-3880 build_csv_kwargs, auth.py:20-25 login); (5) uploaded files via request.files (views.py:3888-3891); (6) CLI options of the 'dtale' click command (dtale/cli/script.py 22 @click.option decorators plus dynamically generated --<loader>-path/--<loader>-proxy options from LOADER_PROPS via clickutils.py loader_options :87-97); (7) environment variables (DTALE_CONFIG, DTALE_CLI_LOADERS, JUPYTERHUB_SERVICE_PREFIX, DTALE_MIN/MAX_PORT, WERKZEUG_RUN_MAIN, VSCODE_PID/VSCODE_INJECTION; 10 os.environ.get sites + 1 request.environ.get); (8) the dtale.ini configuration file (config.py:23 config.read(path), located via DTALE_CONFIG or $HOME/.config/dtale.ini). Outbound network access is issued exclusively through requests.get (5 call sites); the web-upload -> loader_func -> handle_path -> requests.get chain is the dominant SSRF-relevant flow (url AND proxy both attacker-supplied).

extraction.executionModel: codeql query run + codeql bqrs decode (raw multi-column candidate tables); NOT database analyze / SARIF. Plain multi-column select queries on purpose: @kind problem is the wrong shape for candidate tables and @kind table is not assumed to exist.
columnContract: node - candidate AST node (location-backed, decodes as file:line:col)
callableName - wrapper/parameter/attribute/API member name at the candidate
receiver - syntactic receiver hint (base name of the object expression, enclosing class name for function rows, '' if none)

moduleHint - external module name for API rows ('requests', 'urllib.parse') or dotted python module path of the candidate (variable intentionally named moduleHint; 'module' is not a valid QL variable name)
argIndex - 0-based positional index of the input/URL-carrying argument where applicable, -1 when not applicable
file - absolute path via AstNode.getLocation().getFile().getAbsolutePath() (AstNode.getFile() does not exist)
matchKind - 'api' (CodeQL-resolved real API call via API graphs) or 'ast' (syntax-level match)
extraction.csvFieldOrder: node,role,callableName,flowKind,receiver,moduleHint,argIndex,file,line,matchKind (identical to the earlier SSRF/core, mlflow and maltrail extraction CSVs)
sourceQueryFamilies: http_query_arg_call - calls of get_str_arg/get_int_arg/get_float_arg/get_bool_arg/get_json_arg (ast; argIndex 1 = position of the literal query-parameter-name argument, the tainted value is the call result)
request_json - request.json.get(...) calls (ast, argIndex 0) and bare request.json attribute reads not already covered by a .get call (ast, argIndex -1)
request_form - request.form.get(...) calls (ast, argIndex 0), request.form[...] subscripts (ast, argIndex -1) and bare request.form attribute reads (ast, argIndex -1)
cli_arg - click.option(...) decorator/dynamic option-construction calls under dtale/cli (ast, argIndex 0 = option name argument)
env - os.environ.get(...) / request.environ.get(...) calls (ast, argIndex 0) and os.environ[...] subscripts (ast, argIndex -1)
sinkQueryFamilies: arg/api - requests.get calls resolved through API graphs (alias-aware; argIndex 0 = URL argument)
arg/ast - syntactic requests.get(...) shapes (intentionally redundant with the api family; argIndex 0)
internal_path_funnel - handle_path(...) call sites: the shared remote-fetch funnel (ast, argIndex 0 = path argument)
internal_loader_wrapper - functions whose body calls handle_path (csv/json/excel loader_func: the /web-upload and CLI entry into the funnel)
internal_fetch_wrapper - functions whose body directly issues a requests.get fetch (handle_path, load_zip, kill, is_up, app reaper closure _func)

url_parse - urllib.parse.parse_qsl/urlencode/quote/unquote references (charts.py:91-94/:199, utils.py:49/:56 PY2/PY3 shims): URL parse/encode construction, NOT final network I/O; emitted only as summary-labeling candidates
extraction.excludedPaths: tests/, test_*.py, conftest.py, dtale-db (nested CodeQL database), ssrf_analyzer.py, ssrf_precise_analyzer.py (pre-existing analysis artifacts at the source root)

uncoveredCases: pandas IO URL fetching: pd.read_csv/read_json/read_excel (csv_loader.py:31, json_loader.py:44, excel_loader.py:33) receive whatever handle_path returns, and pd.read_parquet (parquet_loader.py:33) receives the raw 'path' WITHOUT handle_path - pandas itself performs remote http(s) reads for URL paths inside the library. This is library-internal behavior not provable from this source tree, so these call sites are not emitted as sinks; listed as a possible coverage gap (a URL reaching pd.read_parquet directly from /web-upload parquet branch views.py:3956 is fetchable only via pandas internals).
dash callback inputs (35+ @app.callback sites): user-controlled chart parameters with no network path in this tree - not extracted (no source-to-network propagation provable).
